summary: This tutorial details the `RuntimeDeterministicAdapter` architecture used in HyperFrames to synchronize and seek diverse animation runtimes (GSAP, Lottie, CSS, WAAPI, Three.js, TypeGPU) onto a single deterministic video clock. The submission provides concrete TypeScript interface definitions, registry strategies, and handling for edge cases like GSAP's `_tTime` render skip. Grounding confirms the referenced repository and adapter implementations align with the architectural documentation provided.
strengths: Comprehensive and clearly structured technical documentation of the adapter architecture.
Provides concrete TypeScript interface definitions and practical examples for each runtime integration.
Addresses subtle runtime quirks, such as GSAP's totalTime render skip and WebGPU synchronization.
Directly backed by a verified, open-source codebase (HyperFrames) with explicit commit references.
weaknesses: Some adapter interactions (like Anime.js v4 integration limitations) are acknowledged as inert or restricted, which might require additional developer overhead.
Assumes familiarity with the broader HyperFrames architecture and composition model.
suggestions: Include a minimal full-code example demonstrating a composition utilizing three different runtimes simultaneously.
Expand briefly on error handling strategies when an individual adapter throws during a seek pass.

claims.text: HyperFrames owns the clock. Animation libraries do not play. Each motion runtime implements RuntimeDeterministicAdapter with discover, seek, and pause, plus optional duration inference and readiness.
GSAP 3.x skips a render when totalTime equals _tTime, so the adapter nudges then seeks.
Three.js and TypeGPU receive hf-seek CustomEvents.

novelty_vs_existing.title: An HTML composition contract for deterministic video
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses specifically on the runtime adapter interface and multi-library synchronization mechanics (GSAP, Lottie, Three.js, etc.) rather than the general HTML data-composition schema.
